summary:
H.R. 8580, the “Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025,” provides appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025, for military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and related agencies. The bill operates by making specified sums available from the Treasury, subject to terms, conditions, and transfer authorities.

**Title I — Department of Defense.** Appropriates funds for military construction for the Army, Navy and Marine Corps, Air Force, Defense-Wide, Army and Air National Guard, and the reserve components, generally to remain available until September 30, 2029. Each account caps amounts for study, planning, design, and architect-engineer services and permits exceeding those caps only with committee notification. Specific amounts are earmarked by reference to tables in the accompanying committee report. The NATO Security Investment Program receives $433,864,000 (available until expended). The Department of Defense Base Closure Account receives $547,961,000 (available until expended). Family housing construction and operation accounts are appropriated, with availability periods as specified.

Administrative provisions (Sections 101–133) impose numerous restrictions and authorities: e.g., prohibition on cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts over $25,000 without Secretarial approval (Sec. 101); advance of funds to FHWA for access roads (Sec. 103); limitations on land purchases exceeding appraised value (Sec. 105); prohibitions on new bases without specific appropriation (Sec. 104), on transfer of activities under minor construction (Sec. 107), and on procurement of steel where U.S. producers were denied competition (Sec. 108). Section 117 authorizes transfers to Family Housing and Unaccompanied Housing Improvement Funds subject to 30‑day (or 14‑day electronic) notification. Section 118 authorizes transfers from the Base Closure Account to the Homeowners Assistance Program fund under 42 U.S.C. § 3374. Section 120 appropriates Ford Island Improvement Account amounts. Section 121 permits transfers of expired unobligated balances to “Foreign Currency Fluctuations, Construction, Defense.” Section 124 provides additional amounts across accounts ($357 million total) for projects on the military departments’ unfunded priority lists, conditioned on prior authorization and an expenditure plan within 60 days. Sections 128–132 appropriate additional sums for laboratory facilities, child development centers, barracks, and demolition, each conditioned on submission (and in some cases prior approval) of expenditure plans. Section 133 prohibits use of funds to close or realign Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, Cuba.

**Title II — Department of Veterans Affairs.** Makes appropriations for the Veterans Benefits Administration (Compensation and Pensions; Readjustment Benefits; Veterans Insurance and Indemnities; Housing Benefit Program Fund; Vocational Rehabilitation Loans; Native American Veteran Housing Loan Program; General Operating Expenses). The Compensation and Pensions account provides $9.82 billion (fiscal year 2025 advance) and $204.48 billion (to become available October 1, 2025). Readjustment Benefits and Insurance accounts similarly include advance appropriations for fiscal year 2026. The Veterans Health Administration receives appropriations for Medical Services ($75.039 billion, available October 1, 2025), Medical Community Care ($34 billion), Medical Support and Compliance ($12.7 billion), Medical Facilities ($9.7 billion), and Medical and Prosthetic Research ($923.5 million), with specified periods of availability and portions for longer-term obligations. The Cost of War Toxic Exposures Fund receives $22.8 billion, available October 1, 2025, until expended. Construction accounts include Major Projects ($2.069 billion, with specific obligation deadlines) and Minor Projects ($380.5 million). Grants for State Extended Care Facilities and Veterans Cemeteries are appropriated.

Administrative provisions (Sections 201–261) authorize transfers among certain accounts, subject to committee approval for amounts above specified thresholds (e.g., Sec. 202, 218, 219, 220, 228, 229). Section 208 requires insurance fund reimbursement of administrative costs. Section 231 mandates hotline requirements and a study. Section 232 prohibits deviation from a specified breast cancer screening guidance through January 1, 2026. Section 233 authorizes fertility treatment and adoption reimbursement for certain veterans. Section 235 exempts certain tribally-owned contractors from Section 842 of Public Law 109‑115. Section 236 requires discontinuation of Social Security numbers for authentication. Section 242 provides Inspector General access rights and reporting. Section 246 restricts canine, feline, and non-human primate research, requiring Secretarial certification and a plan to end such research by March 9, 2026. Several policy riders restrict funds for abortion (Sec. 255), gender affirming care (Sec. 256), flying certain flags (Sec. 257), Special Modes of Transportation rule (Sec. 258), COVID-19 vaccination mandate (Sec. 259), reporting certain VA beneficiaries as mentally defective for NICS (Sec. 261, 427), and other specified executive orders, DEI activities, and critical race theory (Sections 414, 415, 417).

**Title III — Related Agencies.** Appropriates funds for the American Battle Monuments Commission, U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims, Arlington National Cemetery and Soldiers’ and Airmen’s Home National Cemetery (salaries and construction), and the Armed Forces Retirement Home Trust Fund, including a general fund transfer.

**Title IV — General Provisions.** Contains government-wide restrictions and authorities, including prohibitions on funds for named executive orders, diversity-equity-inclusion training, COVID-19 mask mandates, and certain climate-related actions (Sec. 414–420). Section 416 prohibits discriminatory action based on beliefs about marriage. Section 421 restricts procurement of certain Chinese-linked IT equipment by the VA. The Act may be cited as the “Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025.”
